title: The hour before the school bus: How connected technology can help calm the morning rush
summary: How smart-home technology can calm the morning rush, helping families automate routines, reduce distractions and start the day with confidence.
body_markdown:
The hour before the kids leave for school can be a scramble for even the most organized families.


Lunches are being packed. A permission slip is sitting unsigned on the kitchen counter. The dog still needs to go outside. Parents are watching the clock while mentally juggling pickup schedules, after-school activities and their own morning commute.


It's not usually one big problem that creates stress. It's dozens of small decisions competing for attention at the same time.


Did someone lock the back door? Are the lights still on upstairs? Will the house be comfortable when everyone gets home? What if I forget something important?


As families look for ways to simplify busy routines during the school year, many are turning to connected technology to automate everyday tasks and reduce some of the mental load of managing a household.


"Understanding your routine and being able to adapt to it is really important for us at ADT," said James Knox, ADT's Director of Product Management. "Our goal is to recognize when something falls outside a home's normal routine and help homeowners decide whether action is needed."


That philosophy reflects a broader shift in how families use smart-home technology. Instead of simply monitoring what happens at home, connected devices can help households prepare for the day ahead, automate recurring tasks and reduce the number of things parents need to think about before walking out the door.


Here are three ways connected technology can help make hectic mornings a little easier.


### Put routine tasks on autopilot


During a busy morning, every task someone doesn't have to remember is one less thing competing for attention.


Connected-home automations can help handle many of the small actions that often become last-minute worries. Families can[schedule lights to turn off](https://www.adt.com/resources/automated-lighting-guide) after everyone leaves, automatically arm their system as the house empties or adjust temperatures before the day begins.


Using the ADT+ app, homeowners can create routines around how their family actually lives, with schedules that differ between weekdays, weekends and school breaks.


Rather than wondering whether the house was secured while rushing from school drop-off to work, parents can have confidence that those tasks happened automatically.


### Stay connected without constant check-ins


Even during the morning rush, families are rarely all moving on the same schedule.


One child may leave early for band practice. A teenager might miss the bus and head back home. A grandparent could stop by while everyone is away.


Connected cameras and video doorbells can help families stay informed without requiring texts, calls or constant check-ins.


Through the ADT+ app, homeowners can receive notifications from devices such as doorbell cameras and see who's at the door from virtually anywhere. Two-way audio also allows family members to communicate with visitors or children who arrive home later in the day.


For households that regularly coordinate with trusted family members, caregivers or service providers,[Trusted Neighbor](https://www.adt.com/trusted-neighbor) † can simplify access by allowing temporary or scheduled entry directly through the ADT+ app.


The result is fewer interruptions and more visibility into what's happening at home throughout the day.


### Catch the things busy mornings make easy to miss


The faster a morning moves, the easier it is to overlook something.


A garage door gets left open. A window that's normally closed remains open after everyone leaves. A routine part of the morning simply doesn't happen.


The ADT+ app's[Unusual Activity Alerts](https://newsroom.adt.com/innovations/adt-expands-intelligent-home-features-with-unusual-activity-alerts) feature is designed to identify activity that falls outside a home's normal patterns and draw attention to situations that may deserve a second look. Using information from connected devices such as ADT door and window sensors, the feature can help surface issues that might otherwise go unnoticed.


According to Knox, the objective isn't to create more alerts. It's to help homeowners focus on the alerts that matter most.


"The most effective smart-home experiences aren't the ones that create the most notifications," Knox said. "They're the ones that help homeowners quickly understand what matters and decide whether action is needed."


### When a busy day becomes something more


Sometimes, however, a situation requires more than a notification. That's where[professional monitoring](https://newsroom.adt.com/employee-experience/what-makes-adt-monitoring-different-5-reasons-it-stands-out) provides an additional layer of support.


ADT's network of company-operated monitoring centers is staffed 24/7/365 by trained professionals who can help when alarm events occur* — whether you’re home or not.


For Knox, that's where technology and people work best together.


"Professional monitoring gives homeowners reassurance that someone is looking out for them,” Knox said. “It provides confidence that support is available when human expertise and response are needed.”


### A calmer start to the day


No technology can eliminate the realities of family life. There will still be forgotten lunchboxes, last-minute schedule changes and mornings when everyone is running late.


But when fewer routine tasks require attention, families can spend less time worrying about what they may have forgotten and more time focusing on getting where they need to go.


Sometimes peace of mind doesn't come from adding more information. It comes from having fewer things to think about before the school bus arrives.
